title: TwinVPN — Connection outcomes
description: The four questions ADR-0015 says matter: connection outcome by NAT class pair, relay incidence, time-to-first-byte, and both address families side by side. NOTE THE DATA SOURCE: the outcome and NAT panels read Tier-2 AGGREGATE counters (ADR-0015 §11.1), which are OFF BY DEFAULT and OPT-IN. §13 records that this makes them a BIASED SAMPLE - privacy-motivated users decline - so they are for regression DETECTION, never for absolute rates. A decision must never be gated on them alone.

list.name: address_family
list.description: ADR-0010 R1: one story covering both families. A panel filtered to v4 alone is an incomplete answer (ADR-0015 O-09), which is why All is the default.

panels.title: Outcome by NAT class pair (Tier-2 aggregate — biased sample)
Connection outcome by NAT class pair
panels.description:
docs/testing-strategy.md §3.6 classifies pairs as DIRECT_EXPECTED or RELAY_EXPECTED, and release blocker B-6 fires when a DIRECT_EXPECTED pair falls back to RELAYED or a RELAY_EXPECTED pair claims WAN_DIRECT. This panel is where that shows up in the field rather than in the lab.

ARCHITECTURE CONFLICT, reported not resolved: ADR-0015 §11.1's Tier-2 tuple lists a single `nat_class`, but a PAIR needs two. This panel queries twinvpn_nat_class_local and twinvpn_nat_class_remote; if the disposition is that Tier 2 carries only one, this panel loses its x-axis and the question moves to the lab.

panels.title: Relay incidence — share of sessions that are RELAYED
panels.description: R-01 wants a direct path whenever the network permits one; R-02 makes relay fallback automatic and CONCURRENT rather than a post-timeout retry, so a relayed session is not a failure. A RISING share is the signal - it means direct paths that used to work stopped working. ADR-0006 §11.10 makes RELAYED -> WAN_DIRECT upgrade opportunistic, so persistent relay share is the number to watch, not instantaneous.

panels.title: Relay flows bound, per region and failure domain
panels.description: Infrastructure-side counter, NOT Tier-2. ADR-0015 §9 restricts relay labels to the five-dimension allowlist; there is deliberately no per-session or peer-pair label here, which is O-13 working as intended and is why this panel can show load but can never show a user.

panels.title: Time to first byte — p50 / p90 / p99, by address family
panels.description: Both families, always (docs/testing-strategy.md V5). ADR-0005 §11.4 races carriages with a staggered start (R-UDP at 0 ms, R-QUIC at +250 ms, R-TLS at +750 ms) and cancels the losers at 2 s, and ADR-0002 §11.2 gives the control ladder 3 s at rung 1. A p99 above ~2 s means the relay carriage ladder ran to exhaustion; a p50 that diverges BETWEEN FAMILIES is the asymmetry ADR-0010 R1 forbids.

panels.title: Control-plane transport rung in use (ADR-0002 §11.2)
panels.description: Rung 1 is QUIC+HTTP/3 on UDP:443. Falling to any rung below 1 MUST be surfaced, and each fall emits its own code: CONTROL.TRANSPORT_DEGRADED_TCP, CONTROL.TRANSPORT_DEGRADED_POLL, CONTROL.TRANSPORT_VIA_PROXY. ADR-0002 §14 condition 1 makes rung-1 attach success below 90% a trigger to revisit the ADR, so this panel is the one that decides that.
